checks.title: Data quality: measure inputs
checks.summary: Measures the declared dataset before any rule is proposed: per-column types, nulls, distincts and tails; row counts, key uniqueness, duplicate and orphan rows, and per-period drift signals; and, separately, what the data says about every expectation the owner stated. Columns the safe-use boundary names sensitive are reported as counts and masked examples only. A source that cannot be reached is recorded as unverified, never invented.
checks.description:
Profile the declared dataset for real, BEFORE proposing any rule. Read or query the data directly (sample only when the full scan is genuinely infeasible, and say so with the sample size and how it was drawn) and report what is actually there. Per column: name, physical type, null count and null percentage, distinct count, and for numerics/dates the min, max, and the p01/p50/p99 so an implausible tail is visible. Across the dataset: total row count; whether the declared key columns ARE unique at the declared grain, with the exact duplicate row count; exact-duplicate whole rows; REFERENTIAL ORPHANS — for each relationship implied by the brief or visible in the columns, the count of rows whose reference has no match, with the parent named; DRIFT SIGNALS — where the data is partitioned by time or arrives in batches, the per-period row count, null rate and mean of the key measures, so a step change or a silently emptied period is visible; and concrete data-quality issues (sentinel values like 1970-01-01, -1 or 9999, mixed encodings, timezone ambiguity, silently truncated strings, soft-deleted or test rows, numbers stored as text, trailing-whitespace keys). Then, SEPARATELY, take each expectation the owner stated in the brief and record what the data says about it: supported, contradicted, or not-checkable-yet, with the observed number — this is the bridge from belief to evidence, and it must not be skipped for an expectation that turns out to be uncomfortable. Respect the safe-use boundary: report counts and masked or offset-based examples for any column named sensitive there, never raw values. If a source cannot be reached, mark it verified:false and say what is missing — NEVER invent a profile, never round a number you did not observe. Write data-profile.json using checks.sh; the file must contain this JSON: {"dataset":{"name":str,"format":str,"verified":bool,"rowCount":number,"scanned":"full"|"sample","sampleNote":str},"columns":[{"name":str,"type":str,"nullCount":number,"nullPct":number,"distinctCount":number,"min":str,"max":str,"p01":str,"p99":str}],"candidateKeys":[{"columns":[str],"unique":bool,"duplicateRows":number}],"duplicateRows":number,"referentialOrphans":[{"child":str,"parent":str,"orphanRows":number}],"driftSignals":[{"dimension":str,"observation":str,"periods":[{"period":str,"rows":number,"note":str}]}],"expectationEvidence":[{"expectation":str,"status":"supported"|"contradicted"|"not-checkable","observed":str}],"issues":[str],"openQuestions":[str]}.
Create a reproducible checks.sh that reads the declared data and writes data-profile.json. Run exactly sh checks.sh as a separate SDK command. Confirm required inputs, parse the declared key-column list (none requires candidate columns), and check every named column against the real header before profiling. An unreadable named file or missing key column must fail. Include the source identity, query/code, full-versus-sample scope and observed counts. Use only the connections and tool setup explicitly permitted for this step. If a required engine or source is unavailable under those permissions, fail with the missing requirement.
produces: checks.sh, a reproducible program that reads the declared data and writes the profile; the agent runs exactly `sh checks.sh` as a separate SDK command.
data-profile.json: dataset identity and scan scope, per-column counts, candidate keys, duplicate rows, referential orphans, drift signals, expectation evidence, issues and open questions.
recomputes: Observes the exact `sh checks.sh` execution in the SDK sandbox and rejects a program or output inventory that changed around it.
Requires a verified source with a positive row count, and either a stated full scan or a sample with its size and method.
Checks every declared key column appears among the measured columns, and that column names are distinct.
Rejects null or distinct counts larger than the row count, and a candidate key whose unique flag disagrees with its duplicate-row count.
Requires at least one expectation-evidence row, each with an allowed status (supported, contradicted, not-checkable) and an observed value.
proves: The named program ran to completion in the sandbox and produced a profile whose counts are internally consistent.
The declared key columns exist in the real source header and were measured at the declared grain.
Every expectation the owner stated is answered with an observed number rather than quietly dropped.
doesNotProve: That the reported numbers describe the real dataset: the host reads the model's report, it does not re-query the source.
That the profile is complete; an issue, orphan or drift signal nobody looked for is simply absent.
That a sampled scan represents the population. The sample note is recorded, not validated.

checks.title: Data quality: review plan
checks.summary: Turns the measured profile and the owner's stated expectations into an executable rule set: one rule for every expectation, rules for the problems the profile actually found, and the structural rules the declared grain implies. Each rule carries its assertion, scope, threshold with justification, severity and the named downstream consequence that earns it. An expectation that cannot be evaluated per row is listed as unexpressible with its reason. Nothing runs here; the rules are for a person to approve.
checks.description:
Propose the quality rule set from the MEASURED profile and the owner's stated expectations. Rules to derive: (1) one rule for EVERY expectation in the brief — an expectation that cannot be expressed as an executable assertion is still listed, with expressible:false and why, so nothing the owner believes is silently dropped; (2) rules for the problems the profile actually found (duplicate keys, orphans, sentinel values, implausible tails, empty periods) even where the owner did not think to ask; (3) the structural rules the grain implies — key uniqueness and key non-nullity at the declared grain. Each rule carries: a stable id (kebab-case); the human statement; the dimension (completeness | uniqueness | validity | consistency | referential | timeliness); the executable assertion, written as the SQL predicate or expression that identifies a VIOLATING row (so the check counts violations rather than merely returning a boolean); the scope (which table/file and which subset of rows it applies to); the threshold — the violation count or rate above which the rule fails, WITH its justification, and set from the profile rather than from optimism: a rule whose threshold is set above the violation rate the profile already measured is a rule designed to pass, and is forbidden; the severity (blocker | major | minor) and — this is the part that earns the severity — WHY: which downstream decision, report or model breaks when this rule fails, in one concrete sentence. A severity with no named consequence is not a severity, it is a mood. Order the rules by severity, then by the violation rate the profile suggests. Note explicitly which rules are expected to FAIL on today's data based on the profile — an audit whose rules were all quietly tuned to pass tells the owner nothing. Respect the safe-use boundary in the assertions and in any example the rule would surface. Write quality-rules.json with this JSON: {"rules":[{"id":str,"rule":str,"dimension":str,"assertion":str,"scope":str,"threshold":{"kind":"count"|"rate","value":number,"justification":str},"severity":"blocker"|"major"|"minor","why":str,"expressible":bool,"derivedFrom":"expectation"|"profile"|"grain","expectedToFail":bool,"profileEvidence":str,"evidenceRequired":str}],"unexpressible":[{"expectation":str,"why":str}],"coverageNotes":str}. THRESHOLD DISCIPLINE (the observed systematic failure): when an owner expectation carries no approved allowance and the profile has measured a violation rate, the threshold comes from the OWNER'S stated boundary — or zero to keep the defect visible — NEVER from the measured rate. Setting any threshold equal to (or within 10% of) a profile-measured rate is designing the rule to pass and will be rejected; if you believe the measured rate IS the right allowance, mark the rule expressible with threshold zero and record the proposed allowance in its justification for the human to approve explicitly. DENOMINATOR DISCIPLINE: a rule's scorecard `checked` count must equal the rows actually evaluated per-row at the declared grain — never 1 for an aggregate/metadata check and never the row count of a check that did not examine rows. If an expectation cannot be evaluated per-row at the declared grain (e.g. uniqueness with no usable key, timeliness with no arrival evidence), it is UNEXPRESSIBLE: record it in unexpressible[] with the reason — do not emit it as a rule with a synthetic denominator. KEY-UNIQUENESS RECONCILIATION (the two disciplines above collide without this): grain-key uniqueness and key non-nullity ARE per-row expressible whenever any declared OR constructible (provisional/composite) key exists — emit them as rules over that key, naming it provisional if it is one, with checked = rows examined. They belong in unexpressible[] ONLY when no per-row identity can be constructed at all, and then the entry must say what identity was sought and why none exists. EVIDENCE REQUIRED (what makes an evidence-gap distinguishable from a violation later): every rule states, in evidenceRequired, the evidence or metadata the data must CARRY for the rule to mean anything — the declared timezone of a timestamp column, the arrival/load timestamp a freshness rule compares against, the reference table a referential rule joins to, the unit a range rule assumes. Write it as the concrete thing that must be present, not as a hope. A rule whose evidenceRequired is absent from the data does not condemn the data; it condemns what is known about the data, and the executor will classify its failure as an evidence-gap rather than a violation on that basis. Where the profile already shows the evidence is missing, say so in profileEvidence so the human approving the rule knows they are approving a rule that will report a gap.
Use one or more unique executable rules; one complete rule is sufficient. Assign severity from the stated consequence; an audit need not contain a blocker. Read the earlier profile step and its data-profile.json. Add expectations:[str] on every rule, using the EXACT expectation strings from profile.expectationEvidence that the rule covers; unmatched expectations must appear in unexpressible[]. Do not run the proposed rules before approval.
produces: quality-rules.json rules[]: id, statement, dimension, the executable assertion selecting violating rows, scope, threshold with justification, severity, why and the expectations covered.
unexpressible[]: every expectation that cannot be an executable per-row assertion, each with the reason it cannot be one.
coverageNotes describing how the rule set covers the profile and the brief.
recomputes: Reads the earlier data-profile.json and requires every profile expectation to be covered by a rule or listed as unexpressible with a reason.
Requires distinct kebab-case rule ids, an allowed severity, an explicit count or rate threshold with its justification, and expressible:true on every rule.
Requires each rule to state its dimension, assertion, scope, why, profileEvidence and evidenceRequired as nonempty text.
Runs nothing: this step is a proposal, so the host executes no rule program and reads no data.
proves: Every expectation the profile recorded is either an executable rule or an explicitly justified omission.
Each proposed rule carries a threshold, a severity and a named consequence a person can approve or reject.
doesNotProve: That a rule is correct, or that its assertion selects the rows its statement describes.
That a threshold is reasonable: the host checks that one exists and is justified in prose, not that the number is right.
That the rules would pass or fail; nothing has been run against the data at this step.

checks.title: Data quality: check results
checks.summary: Executes the approved rules against the declared data and emits a scorecard: per rule the units examined, violations, rate, the threshold comparison, and whether a failure is a data violation or an evidence gap. The dataset is read-only — this step audits, it never repairs. A seeded-violation fixture must trip an approved rule, so a rule that silently passes everything is exposed. Finding violations is the audit succeeding; they belong in the scorecard, not in the exit code.
checks.description:
Execute the APPROVED rule set against the declared data and emit the scorecard under ./. WRITE BOUNDARY: this node audits, it does not repair. The declared dataset is READ-ONLY — no UPDATE, no DELETE, no schema change, no 'cleaned' copy written back to the source; every byte you write goes under ./. Emit: (1) ./rules/<rule_id>.sql (or .py where SQL cannot express it) — one file per approved rule, each SELECTing the violating rows so the count is derived from the same query that could show them; (2) ./fixtures/ — a small seeded input set AND a SEEDED-VIOLATION variant in which a known number of rows deliberately breaks one approved executable rule, regardless of its severity, so a rule that silently passes everything is exposed; (3) ./checks.sh — a POSIX sh script that RUNS every approved rule against the FULL declared data and writes quality-scorecard.json as {"dataset":{"identity":str,"rows":number,"scanned":"full"|"sample","sampleNote":str},"rules":[{"id":str,"rule":str,"dimension":str,"severity":str,"class":"violation"|"evidence-gap","checked":number,"checkedUnit":str,"violations":number,"rate":number,"threshold":str,"pass":bool,"query":str,"missingEvidence":str,"examples":[str]}],"notRun":[{"id":str,"why":str}],"negativeCase":{"id":"seeded-violation","rule":str,"seededRows":number,"detectedRows":number,"tripped":bool},"bySeverity":{"blocker":{"failed":number,"total":number},"major":{"failed":number,"total":number},"minor":{"failed":number,"total":number}},"byClass":{"violation":{"failed":number,"total":number},"evidence-gap":{"failed":number,"total":number}},"passed":number,"failed":number}.  NON-NEGOTIABLE — EVERY RULE, FULL DATA: every approved rule is executed against the DECLARED data from the context block, and those observed counts are the scorecard's primary evidence; the fixtures exist ONLY as the seeded negative case. A rule that cannot run is recorded in notRun with the reason and counts as a failure of the audit, never as a silent omission and never as a pass. Scanning a sample instead of the full data is permitted ONLY when a full scan is genuinely infeasible, and then dataset.scanned must say 'sample' with the sample size and method — a rate reported from a sample and presented as the full population is a dishonest scorecard. UNITS ON EVERY DENOMINATOR: `checked` is a bare number and different rules count different things — a row-level predicate counts ROWS, a schema or per-file rule counts FILES, a referential rule may count KEYS. Every rule row therefore carries `checkedUnit` naming what `checked` counts in the plural noun a reader would use ("rows", "files", "keys", "columns", "partitions"); a rule row without checkedUnit is an incomplete report. The unit travels with the number everywhere it is written: the one-line summary, the rule row, and every example string. PLURALISE AGAINST THE COUNT, not against the field name — "1 violating row", "6 of 6 files", never "1 violating rows". EXAMPLES STATE FILE-GRAIN FACTS AS FACTS: where the unit is not rows, the examples name the thing and what was observed about it ("2025-03.csv has 20 columns, the brief declares 21"), never a fabricated row count and never a row offset the rule never looked at. REPORT FORMAT: per rule, {rule, checked (how many of checkedUnit the rule actually examined), checkedUnit, violations, rate (violations/checked), severity, class, pass} — a pass with checked:0, or violations with no rate, is an incomplete report; the pass verdict is the threshold comparison, computed, never asserted. EVIDENCE-GAP CLASSIFICATION (the observed systematic misreport): every rule is classified as either a VIOLATION or an EVIDENCE-GAP, and the two mean different things. class:"violation" means the data was examined and the rows genuinely break the rule — that is a defect in the data. class:"evidence-gap" means the rule could not be evidenced because the metadata or context it needs is ABSENT: the timestamp column carries no declared timezone so 'no future timestamps' cannot be evaluated without assuming one; there is no arrival or load timestamp so freshness has nothing to measure against; no column declares the unit or currency a range rule assumes, so the range can only be judged against a guess. (A rule that could not run at all — the reference table is missing, the query errored — is NOT an evidence-gap: it belongs in notRun, which is a failure of the audit.) The distinction is about MISSING EVIDENCE, not about difficulty or inconvenience: a rule you simply did not like the result of is a violation. An evidence-gap rule still reports its real checked count and its real failing-row count and still fails when it fails — nothing is hidden — but it also carries missingEvidence naming exactly what is absent and what supplying it would settle, and it is rolled up separately in byClass so 3,000,000 rows lacking a timezone declaration never reads as 3,000,000 rows of bad data. bySeverity is UNCHANGED by this: severity is about consequence and is rolled up over every rule regardless of class. Where a rule was approved with evidenceRequired and that evidence is present, it is a violation-class rule and stays one. NOTES DEFINE WHAT THEY COIN: any `notes` or `missingEvidence` field is read by someone who was not in the run. Define a term where you coin it, in the same sentence ("the five rules that report missing evidence rather than data violations ('evidence gaps')"), and never introduce three undefined terms in one clause. Where a note describes a threshold, SAY WHICH SIDE OF IT THE BOUNDARY CASE LANDS ON — "a difference of exactly one cent PASSES, because the tolerance is inclusive" — because "remains within the approved tolerance" does not tell a reader whether the boundary case passed or failed. SAFE USE: examples must respect the safe-use boundary — masked, hashed or offset-based for any sensitive column named there — and no example may reproduce enough rows to reconstitute the dataset. TOOLCHAIN: use the engine and interpreter already available in this SDK sandbox. Only use network access or install dependencies when explicitly permitted in this step; follow the supplied connection and tool-runtime settings. If a required dependency or source is unavailable, fail with its exact requirement. Never hard-code a passing result, never embed credentials (read connection settings from the environment), and never soften a threshold the human approved — if a threshold now looks wrong, the scorecard says so in notes and still reports the verdict as approved. EXIT-CODE CONTRACT for checks.sh (the observed systematic failure): finding violations IS the audit succeeding — checks.sh MUST exit 0 whenever every approved rule executed to completion against the full declared data, REGARDLESS of how many violations were found (violations belong in the scorecard, not the exit code). Exit nonzero ONLY when: a rule could not execute, an output artifact could not be written, or the seeded-violation negative fixture fails to trip. checks.sh must also PRINT a one-line summary (rules executed, rules with violations, rules reporting an evidence-gap, total violations) so its log is never empty. RUNTIME BUDGET: when the brief declares one, checks.sh ENFORCES it and fails loudly on overrun — guard the long stages (`timeout <seconds>` where the host has it, otherwise a recorded start time and an explicit elapsed-vs-budget comparison), exit non-zero naming the rule or stage that exceeded and by how much, and record measured elapsed seconds per stage in the scorecard under "timing": {"budget":str,"stages":[{"stage":str,"seconds":number}],"withinBudget":bool}. A budget is never met by quietly switching to a sample, dropping an approved rule, or skipping the seeded negative case — if the honest audit cannot fit, the run fails and says which rule was too slow. When the brief says the budget is unspecified, impose none and invent none. ENVIRONMENT: honour what the brief declares about where this runs — if it states there is no network egress, do not plan an install path that needs one (stay in the stdlib or the engine already present, and say so), if it names an engine or interpreter use that one, and read every connection setting from the environment it names rather than hard-coding it.
Read the previously approved quality-rules.json as immutable input. Write checks.sh and all code/output files directly in this step folder. Run exactly sh checks.sh as a separate SDK command. Complete all file edits before that command; after it finishes, only read the results and hand off. A successful exit must mean all approved rules executed and the negative case tripped; data violations belong in the scorecard and do not make program execution fail. Preserve the approved thresholds even if the data fails them. The negativeCase must identify an approved executable rule of any severity, report tripped:true, a positive seededRows count and detectedRows at least as large as seededRows. The host checks reported counts and rule identity, observes successful program execution and pins the files. These model-authored negative-case outcomes are harness-reported evidence, not independent causal proof that the same rule detected the seeded input; review the actual check code and fixture.
produces: rules/<rule_id>.sql (or .py) : one file per approved rule, each selecting the violating rows the reported count is derived from.
fixtures/ : a small seeded input set and a seeded-violation variant in which a known number of rows breaks one approved executable rule.
checks.sh : runs every approved rule against the full declared data, prints a one-line summary, and exits 0 whenever every rule executed however many violations it found.
quality-scorecard.json : dataset identity and scan scope, per-rule results with checkedUnit, class and verdict, notRun, the negative case, and the severity and class rollups.
recomputes: Observes the exact `sh checks.sh` execution and rejects a program or output inventory that changed around it.
Recomputes each violation rate from that rule's own checked and violation counts and rejects a reported rate that disagrees.
Recomputes each pass verdict from the approved threshold, so the verdict is compared rather than asserted.
Recomputes the bySeverity and byClass rollups and the passed/failed totals from the individual rule rows.
Requires every approved rule to appear exactly once with its approved severity, and notRun to be empty.
Requires the negative case to name an approved rule, report tripped:true, and detect at least as many rows as were seeded.
proves: Every approved rule executed, and each reported verdict follows the approved threshold and the counts printed beside it.
The scorecard's arithmetic is internally consistent: rates, rollups and totals are the host's, not the model's.
doesNotProve: That a query measured what its rule describes: the host reads reported counts and never executes the generated SQL itself.
That the seeded case was detected BY the rule it names. These are model-authored, harness-reported outcomes, not causal proof; inspect the check code and the fixture.
That the data is fit for purpose: a rule nobody proposed is never evaluated, and an evidence gap is a statement about missing metadata, not about clean data.

checks.title: Dataset shift: measure inputs
checks.summary: Measures the baseline and current windows under the same scan mode and one shared bin vocabulary, so a later comparison is between two measured distributions rather than one measured and one remembered. Per declared feature: null and distinct counts, per-bin counts and shares, and how it was binned. Per window: identity, rows, observed period and volume by period. A window that cannot be reached is marked unverified rather than inferred from the other.
checks.description:
Profile BOTH declared windows for real, BEFORE proposing any shift rule, and profile them THE SAME WAY — a comparison is only meaningful when both sides were measured with identical binning, identical filters and identical null handling. Read or query each window directly (sample only when a full scan is genuinely infeasible, and then say so with the sample size and how it was drawn, for BOTH windows). Report, per window: the period actually covered (observed min and max of the time column, not the period the brief claimed), the row count, and per declared feature — physical type, null count and null percentage, distinct count, and the distribution itself. For a NUMERIC feature the distribution is a histogram over bins CUT FROM THE BASELINE (equal-frequency deciles unless the brief says otherwise) plus min/p01/p25/p50/p75/p99/max and the mean; the current window is bucketed into the BASELINE's bin edges, because re-cutting bins per window hides exactly the movement you are looking for. For a CATEGORICAL feature it is the full value vocabulary with per-value counts and shares, so a value present in one window and absent from the other is visible by construction. Also report, across windows: the volume per natural period (day or month) in each window so a step change or a silently empty period is visible, and any SCHEMA difference — a column present in one window and not the other, or with a different physical type — because a schema change is not drift, it is a different dataset, and it must be named as such rather than measured as a large PSI. Note concrete comparability hazards: differing units, a rescaled or re-encoded column, sentinel values (1970-01-01, -1, 9999) appearing in one window only, timezone handling that differs between drops, or a filter that applies to one window and not the other. Respect the safe-use boundary: bucket ranges and counts only for any column named sensitive there, never raw values. If either window cannot be reached, mark it verified:false and say what is missing — NEVER invent a distribution, never round a number you did not observe, and never profile only one window and infer the other. DEPENDENCIES: Follow only the explicit per-step access and temporary tool-runtime permissions. Record pinned versions; do not place environments in delivered files. Write window-profiles.json and return the same JSON: {"baseline":{"identity":str,"verified":bool,"rows":number,"periodObserved":str,"scanned":"full"|"sample","sampleNote":str},"current":{"identity":str,"verified":bool,"rows":number,"periodObserved":str,"scanned":"full"|"sample","sampleNote":str},"features":[{"name":str,"type":str,"whyItMatters":str,"baseline":{"nullPct":number,"distinctCount":number,"bins":[{"bin":str,"count":number,"share":number}],"quantiles":{}},"current":{"nullPct":number,"distinctCount":number,"bins":[{"bin":str,"count":number,"share":number}],"quantiles":{}},"binningNote":str}],"volumeByPeriod":[{"window":"baseline"|"current","period":str,"rows":number}],"schemaDifferences":[{"column":str,"difference":str}],"comparabilityHazards":[str],"toolchain":{},"openQuestions":[str]}.
Create checks.sh that reads both declared windows and writes window-profiles.json. Run exactly sh checks.sh as a separate SDK command, then only read results and hand off. Feature type is the declared logical type (numeric/categorical/timestamp); record physical types separately. Include nullCount for each side; bin counts plus nullCount must equal rows examined. Shares use non-null rows. Use the union categorical vocabulary with identical ordered labels and zero counts for absent values. A schema-incompatible feature may set comparable:false with reason and a matching schemaDifferences entry, instead of invented distributions. The host will attach fixed ../profile/control-spec.json and ../profile/control-counts.json after verifying the profile. Do not create either control file yourself.
produces: checks.sh : profiles both windows and writes the profile; run exactly once as a separate SDK command.
window-profiles.json : both window identities, rows, scan scope and periods; per-feature bins, counts, shares, nulls and distincts; schema differences, comparability hazards and volume by period.
recomputes: Observes the exact `sh checks.sh` execution and rejects a program or output inventory that changed around it.
Recomputes every bin share from its own count, and requires bin counts plus nulls to account for the whole window.
Requires both windows to use the same scan mode and identical bin labels in the same order, so a re-binned feature cannot read as drift.
Requires every declared feature to be profiled exactly once; an uncomparable feature must give a reason and name a matching schema difference.
Writes control-spec.json and control-counts.json itself once the step passes: the seeded control is caller-owned and not designed by the agent.
proves: Both windows were measured under the same scan mode into one comparable bin vocabulary.
The per-bin arithmetic in the profile agrees with the counts reported beside it.
A fixed negative control exists for the later audit that the agent did not design.
doesNotProve: That the reported distributions match the real data: the host checks the report's internal consistency, not the source.
That the bins are meaningful for the feature, or that a sampled window represents its period.
That a feature marked uncomparable truly cannot be compared; the reason is recorded, not verified.

checks.title: Dataset shift: review plan
checks.summary: Proposes one executable drift rule per declared feature from the measured windows, each with its statistic, binning, tolerance and the consequence that earns its severity. A tolerance the owner declared is preserved exactly — statistic, value and unit — and a tolerance the agent suggests is marked as proposed for separate approval. A feature that cannot be compared across both windows belongs in unexpressible with its reason, never in a statistic computed against a synthetic denominator.
checks.description:
Propose the shift rule set from the MEASURED profiles of both windows and the PER-FEATURE table the owner declared in the brief. ONE FEATURE, ONE TOLERANCE: the primary rule preserves THAT feature's own statistic, tolerance and unit. Additional rules need explicitly proposed tolerances with a downstream justification; never borrow a limit from another feature. A feature whose row carries no tolerance does not reach you (the inputs gate refuses the run), so a missing tolerance here means you have invented a rule for a feature nobody declared. Require the selected statistic for every declared feature, preserving its exact owner tolerance and unit. A feature that cannot be expressed as an executable statistic belongs in unexpressible[] with its reason, so none is silently dropped. One selected-statistic rule per comparable feature is sufficient, including PSI for a categorical feature. Category-emergence, volume-drift and executable checks for observed comparability hazards are optional additional proposals. If useful, include them with toleranceOrigin "proposed" and a justified threshold for review under the existing human approval; do not require extra statistics or present their thresholds as owner-declared. Continue reporting period volumes and comparability hazards in the profile whether or not an extra rule is proposed. Each rule carries: a stable id (kebab-case); the feature; the human statement; the statistic (psi | kl | rate-delta | category-emergence | volume-drift); the exact binning or vocabulary it uses, referencing the baseline bin edges from the profile; the tolerance — the value at or above which the feature counts as shifted, in that statistic's unit, WITH where it came from (the primary rule preserves the exact unit declared on the feature's row); toleranceOrigin, which is "declared" when the statistic, number and unit are exactly the ones on that feature's row and "proposed" when you are suggesting one the owner did not state (a rule for a comparability hazard the profile found, say) — a proposed tolerance is approved separately by the human and must never be presented as theirs; the band structure where the brief declares one (watch vs shift); the severity (blocker | major | minor) and — this is the part that earns the severity — WHY: which downstream model, report or decision breaks when this feature moves, in one concrete sentence, taken from the reason the brief gave for that feature. A severity with no named consequence is not a severity, it is a mood. Note explicitly which rules the profiles suggest will trip. Stable data is a valid outcome; do not tune thresholds to manufacture either verdict. Respect the safe-use boundary in the statistics and in any example a rule would surface. Write shift-rules.json and return the same JSON: {"rules":[{"id":str,"feature":str,"rule":str,"statistic":str,"binning":str,"tolerance":{"value":number,"unit":str,"band":str,"source":str},"toleranceOrigin":"declared"|"proposed","severity":"blocker"|"major"|"minor","why":str,"expressible":bool,"derivedFrom":"tolerance"|"profile"|"feature","expectedToTrip":bool,"profileEvidence":str}],"unexpressible":[{"feature":str,"why":str}],"coverageNotes":str}. THRESHOLD DISCIPLINE (the observed systematic failure): a tolerance is either the owner's number for THAT feature (toleranceOrigin "declared") or your proposal for a rule they did not declare (toleranceOrigin "proposed"). There is no third source: not another feature's approved limit, not a default, and above all NEVER the statistic the profile just measured. "Pending explicit feature-specific approval" is not a tolerance - it is a rule with toleranceOrigin "proposed", which the human either approves or sends back. An owner-declared tolerance remains unchanged regardless of the measured statistic; a proposed threshold must be justified by its downstream consequence, never selected merely to pass; if you believe the measured value IS the right allowance, keep the rule at the owner's declared tolerance and record the proposed allowance in tolerance.source for the human to approve explicitly. DENOMINATOR DISCIPLINE: a rule's scorecard `checked` counts must equal the rows actually entering the statistic in EACH window at the declared feature's grain — never 1 for an aggregate statistic, never the row count of a window the check did not read, and never the same number for both windows unless both windows genuinely have it. Rows dropped from a statistic (nulls, an unbinnable value) are reported as excluded with their count, not silently absorbed into a denominator. checks.title: Reconciliation: measure inputs

Also report COMPARABILITY HAZARDS: a measure defined differently on each side per the brief, differing currency or unit, differing rounding precision, a timezone or date-boundary difference that moves rows between periods, differing deduplication, late-arriving or restated rows and any as-of/snapshot timestamp, and a type difference in a key column that would break the join. A measure that means two different things on the two sides is not a discrepancy — it is two measures, and it must be named as such here rather than surface later as an unexplained delta. If either side cannot be reached, mark it verified:false and say what is missing — NEVER invent a total, never round a number you did not observe, and never profile one side and infer the other. DEPENDENCIES: Use only explicitly enabled step access and temporary tool setup. Record pinned versions; keep environments and temporary source copies outside delivered files or remove them before the final checks.sh run completes. Write source-profiles.json and return the same JSON: {"sourceA":{"identity":str,"readPath":str,"verified":bool,"rowsStored":number,"rowsAtGrain":number,"periodObserved":str,"scanned":"full"|"sample","sampleNote":str,"grainUnique":bool,"duplicateKeys":number,"duplicateKeyAmount":number},"sourceB":{same shape},"independentReadPaths":bool,"readPathNote":str,"grain":{"declared":str,"keyColumns":[str]},"measures":[{"name":str,"definitionA":str,"definitionB":str,"totalA":decimal_string,"totalB":decimal_string,"observedDelta":decimal_string,"rowsA":number,"rowsB":number,"droppedA":number,"droppedB":number,"precision":str,"commensurable":bool,"note":str}],"segments":[{"dimension":str,"valuesOnlyInA":[str],"valuesOnlyInB":[str],"valueCountA":number,"valueCountB":number}],"keyCoverage":{"onlyInA":{"keys":number,"amount":decimal_string},"onlyInB":{"keys":number,"amount":decimal_string},"inBoth":{"keys":number}},"observedFilters":[{"side":"A"|"B","filter":str,"evidence":str}],"comparabilityHazards":[str],"toolchain":{},"openQuestions":[str]}.

checks.title: Reconciliation: review plan
checks.summary: Writes one executable equation per reconcilable measure: both sides' totals, the named filter terms that explain the gap with their predicates, sides and directions, and the remainder that stays unexplained. Each equation keeps the tolerance from that measure's own row, in that row's unit. A measure that cannot be computed on both sides at the shared grain is unexpressible with its reason, and a residual bucket with no predicate — timing, misc, rounding — is not a named filter and stays unexplained.
checks.description:
Propose the RECONCILIATION RULES — one accounting equation per measure — from the MEASURED profiles of both sides and the TABLES the owner declared in the brief: one measure row per equation (with the definition each side uses), one tolerance row per measure (with its unit), one known-difference row per named term. ONE MEASURE, ONE TOLERANCE: an equation's tolerance is the number on THAT measure's own tolerance row, in THAT row's unit — never another measure's, never a default, never a value derived from the delta the profile just measured. The shape of every equation is the same and it is the whole point of this recipe: totalA = totalB + (named filter terms) + unexplained. Each equation carries: a stable id (kebab-case); the measure; the human statement of the equation written out with its term names; both sides' totals from the profile; the observed delta; and the TERMS. A term is a NAMED FILTER: it has a kebab-case id prefixed `filter:`, a plain-language name, an EXECUTABLE predicate that selects exactly the rows it claims (a SQL WHERE clause or an equivalent expression over columns that exist in the profile), the side that applies it, the direction it moves the equation, its source (`declared` when it comes from the owner's knownDifferences, `profile` when the profile found it and the owner did not name it), and one sentence on why those rows are legitimately in one dashboard and not the other. NO RESIDUAL BUCKETS: a term called `other`, `timing`, `misc`, `rounding` or `definitional differences` that has no predicate capable of selecting rows is NOT a named filter — it is unexplained, and it must be left in unexplained rather than absorbed as an explained term. Also derive: (1) a PER-SEGMENT BREAKDOWN PLAN — the dimension (or dimensions) the deltas will be reported across, taken from the shared grain, with the rule that per-segment deltas MUST sum to the measure's total delta and per-segment explained amounts MUST sum to the measure's explained amount, so the segment table can be checked against the equation rather than merely accompany it; (2) a GRAIN UNIQUENESS precondition per side, because an equation evaluated over a non-unique grain is arithmetic over a double count; (3) equations or terms for the comparability hazards the profile actually found (an unmatched key set, a timezone boundary moving rows between periods, a rounding-precision difference) even where the owner did not think to name them. A severity with no named consequence is not a severity, it is a mood. Note explicitly which equations the profile suggests will NOT balance — a reconciliation whose tolerances were all set above the gap the data already shows tells the owner nothing. Respect the safe-use boundary in every predicate and example. THRESHOLD DISCIPLINE (the observed systematic failure): a tolerance is either the owner's number for THAT measure (toleranceOrigin "declared") or your proposal for a measure they did not cover (toleranceOrigin "proposed"). There is no third source: not another measure's number, not a default, and above all NEVER the delta the profile just measured. Never widen a declared tolerance to fit the measured gap. A legitimate owner tolerance remains valid even if it is close to the observed discrepancy. DENOMINATOR DISCIPLINE: an equation's report `checkedA` and `checkedB` counts must equal the rows actually entering each side's total at the DECLARED SHARED GRAIN — never 1 for an aggregate total, never the row count of a side the check did not read, and never the same number for both sides unless both sides genuinely have it. Rows dropped from a total (a null measure, an unjoinable key, a row that could not be rolled up) are reported as excluded with their count AND the measure amount they carry, not silently absorbed into the total. A term's amount is likewise the amount its predicate actually selects, with the row count behind it. UNEXPRESSIBLE: if a measure cannot be computed on both sides at the shared grain (it exists on one side only, its two definitions are not commensurable, or the grain cannot be reached on one side), it is UNEXPRESSIBLE: record it in unexpressible[] with the reason — do not emit it as an equation with a synthetic term, a borrowed total, or a tolerance wide enough to swallow the difference. DEFINITION VS DISCREPANCY: a measure whose business definition genuinely differs between the two sides belongs in unexpressible[] or in a term that names the definitional difference with an executable predicate — never in an equation that reports a vocabulary difference as a gap in the data.
Read ../profile/source-profiles.json. Preserve each declared measure and its exact tolerance; do not introduce undeclared measures or propose replacement thresholds. Exact tolerance is zero, and a percentage of a zero total permits zero unexplained only. Do not execute equations before approval.
