Every nonzero segment remainder MUST appear in unexplainedBySegment, including when opposite gaps cancel to a zero measure total, with the amounts summing to unexplained, because 'unexplained: $84,201.55' with no location is a number the owner cannot act on. UNITS ON EVERY DENOMINATOR: checkedA and checkedB are bare numbers, and what they count differs by measure — rows at the shared grain, invoices, files, days. Every measure carries `checkedUnit` naming it in the plural noun a reader would use; a measure without checkedUnit is an incomplete report, and the unit travels with the number into the one-line summary and every example. PLURALISE AGAINST THE COUNT — "1 unmatched key", never "1 unmatched keys". NOTES DEFINE WHAT THEY COIN: define any term you invent in the sentence that coins it, and where a note describes a tolerance, say which side of it the boundary case lands on ("a difference of exactly one cent is WITHIN tolerance"). DENOMINATOR DISCIPLINE: checkedA and checkedB are the rows that actually entered each side's total at the shared grain — never 1 for an aggregate total, never a figure copied from the other side — and rows dropped as null, unjoinable or un-rollable are reported in excludedA/excludedB with their count AND the amount they carry, rather than absorbed into a total. If the grain is not unique on a side, that side's duplicateKeys is reported and the equation reports it rather than quietly summing a double count. SAFE USE: segment labels and examples must respect the safe-use boundary, and no example may reproduce enough rows to reconstitute either source. DEPENDENCIES: Use only explicitly enabled step access and temporary tool setup. Record pinned versions; keep environments and temporary source copies outside delivered files or remove them before the final checks.sh run completes. Never hard-code a passing result, never embed credentials (read connection settings from the environment), and never widen a tolerance the human approved — if a tolerance now looks wrong, the report says so in notes and still reports the verdict as approved. RUNTIME BUDGET: when the brief declares one, checks.sh ENFORCES it and fails loudly on overrun rather than silently reconciling a sample; when the brief declares none, do not invent an additional script budget; the application run deadline still applies. EXIT-CODE CONTRACT for checks.sh (the observed systematic failure): finding discrepancies IS the reconciliation succeeding — checks.sh MUST exit 0 whenever every approved equation executed to completion against the full declared data of both sides, REGARDLESS of how large the deltas turned out to be or how much came back unexplained (a discrepancy belongs in the report, not in the exit code). Exit nonzero ONLY when: an equation could not execute, an output artifact could not be written, either control fails to detect the injected change from the original residual (or absorbs it into a named term), or an equation does not BALANCE ARITHMETICALLY — balanceResidual non-zero, or the per-segment deltas failing to sum to the measure's total delta — because that is the harness contradicting itself rather than a finding about the data. checks.sh must also PRINT a one-line summary (equations executed, measures within tolerance, unexplained amount per measure with its own unit, and control detection per operation) so its log is never empty.
Read ../profile/source-profiles.json and ../rules/recon-rules.json as immutable inputs. Write reconciliation-report.json and delta-table.json in the current folder. Use full-precision decimal strings for all amounts, tolerances and residuals (up to 24 decimal places, no exponent). Each executed term preserves direction as well as id/name/predicate/side/source; explained is the signed sum of amounts using those directions. The real totals must still match the measured profiles; otherwise report source change and fail. Every segment row carries toleranceUnit. Inherit the measure tolerance unless an explicit segmentValue/segmentUnit was approved; percentages use absolute local segment totals, including zero. Set checkedUnit to the exact JSON string "rows" on every primary and control result; these counts are rows at the shared grain. Include explicit exclusions. Report every nonzero segment in unexplainedBySegment, even if opposite segment gaps cancel in the total. Never add unexplained amounts from different measures into one misleading total.
negativeControls is an array containing separate drop-keys and alter-segment cases. seededHow and query are nonempty strings describing the copying and perturbation; do not put objects in these fields. Each case has {id,measure,operation,side:"A",source:"model-fixture",segment,seededHow,query,rowsBefore,rowsAfter,seededDelta,detectedDelta,detected:true,segmentUnexplainedAfter,result}. result is the full recalculated measure-result object for the controlled copy, with the same approved equation metadata, terms and tolerance. seededDelta is signed (the change in A), not a claimed positive magnitude. detectedDelta must equal controlled unexplained minus ORIGINAL unexplained, never merely the controlled remainder. The change must also appear in the named segment relative to its original remainder, while each named term amount and B total remain unchanged. Drop-keys decreases rows; alter-segment preserves rows. The control tests accounting of an injected discrepancy, independently of whether that amount exceeds the owner's tolerance; result.withinTolerance still uses the approved policy. Record the actual keys/amounts under the safe-use boundary and the exact copying/perturbation query. These are model-authored fixtures, not owner-specified controls. A control failure is execution failure. Run exactly sh checks.sh as a separate SDK command after all code edits, then only read results and hand off.
produces: equations/<equation_id>.sql and segments/<equation_id>.sql : one file per approved equation and its segment breakdown.
checks.sh : executes every approved equation and both controls, prints a one-line summary and writes the reports.
reconciliation-report.json : per-measure results with checked and excluded rows, executed terms, explained and unexplained amounts, verdicts, and the negative controls.
delta-table.json : the per-segment rows whose amounts sum to each measure, each with its own tolerance verdict.
recomputes: Observes the exact `sh checks.sh` execution and rejects a program or output inventory that changed around it.
Recomputes the identity A = B + signed terms + unexplained in exact decimal arithmetic and requires the balance residual to be exactly zero.
Recomputes every agreement verdict from the approved tolerance and its declared denominator, at measure and at segment level.
Requires segment amounts and row counts to sum exactly to their measure, and every nonzero segment remainder to be located.
Requires each control to change the unexplained residual by exactly the seeded amount without altering side B or any named term.
Requires results to name the same measured sources, grain and approved equations, with notRun empty.
proves: Every approved equation executed, and its arithmetic identity and tolerance verdict hold under the host's own exact-decimal recomputation.
Each seeded change surfaced in the unexplained remainder and in the declared segment instead of being absorbed.
doesNotProve: That the reported totals came from the real sources: the host recomputes from the numbers in the report, not from the systems.
That the explained terms are the true causes of the difference, only that they are arithmetically consistent.
That the controls establish detection causally: they are model-authored fixtures on a copy, reported by the same program.

checks.title: Pipeline change: measure inputs
checks.summary: Captures the existing pipeline before any change is planned: the declared command executed on a local copy against the declared original data, real baseline output files, the source snapshot identity and as-of evidence, the declared grain and key measurements, and every protected invariant measured with its query and derivation path. At least one protected value is re-derived through a different parse path. An unmeasurable invariant is a failure with a reason, not a quietly reduced contract.
checks.description:
Perform baseline capture ONLY. The overall workflow goal describes later work: do not implement or test the requested change in this step, even on another temporary copy. Keep only baseline/ snapshots, baseline-report.json, optional source-snapshot.json, and flat helper programs or Markdown notes in this step folder. Capture the actual existing pipeline before planning a change. Copy the required code into baseline/, preserving original behavior, and execute the exact declared runCommand there against the declared original data. Redirect all writes into this step. If the original command cannot safely run from a copy, report the blocker and fail; never fabricate a baseline. Capture real baseline model output files under baseline/, not only remembered totals. Report source snapshot identity (file hashes or table versions, sizes/counts and as-of evidence), actual date/sequence bounds and known downstream consumers. Independently derive at least one protected value from raw data through a different parse path, without importing the pipeline's own calculations. No natural key means candidate keys must be measured, not assumed. Preserve all declared invariants and their own kinds/tolerances; record an unmeasurable invariant as a failure with a reason. Do not quietly reduce the contract.
Write baseline-report.json with this exact shape:
{pipeline:{location:exact input pipelineLocation,command:exact input runCommand,executed:true,models:[{name:string,rowCount:positive integer,file:"baseline/<nonempty output file>"}]},snapshot:{identity:string,capturedAt:string},invariants:[{invariant:exact declared name,measure:exact declared measure,kind:"number"|"boolean"|"text",unit:exact declared unit,tolerance:decimal string,baseline:decimal string|boolean|string,measurable:true,query:string,derivationPath:string}],grainCheck:{grain:exact input grain,keyColumns:[declared candidates],duplicateRows:integer,nullKeyRows:integer},independentControl:{invariant:one declared name,value:typed independently computed value,path:string different from that invariant's derivationPath,query:string},consumers:[string],toolchain:{runtime:string,packages:[{name,version}]},issues:[string]}.
Text and boolean invariants use unit exact and tolerance "0"; a numeric exact tolerance also uses "0". Declare any baseline grain failures as measured issues. Create checks.sh to execute the baseline capture, independent control and report writer. Run exactly sh checks.sh as a separate SDK command after editing, then only read results and hand off.
produces: baseline/ : the copied pipeline code and the real baseline model output files it produced, not remembered totals.
checks.sh : executes the baseline capture, the independent control and the report writer.
baseline-report.json : the executed location and command, models with row counts and files, snapshot identity and capture time, every declared invariant with its measured value, and the grain check.
source-snapshot.json : optional identity evidence for the snapshot the baseline ran against.
recomputes: Observes the exact `sh checks.sh` execution and rejects a program or output inventory that changed around it.
Requires the step folder to contain only baseline snapshots, the reports and flat helper programs, so the change cannot be implemented here.
Requires the exact declared pipeline location and run command to be recorded as executed, with every named baseline output file present, unlinked and nonempty.
Requires every declared invariant to be measured exactly once, keeping its declared measure, kind, unit and exact owner tolerance.
Recomputes the independent control against the invariant it names under that invariant's tolerance, and requires its parse path to differ from the invariant's.
proves: The declared command ran on a copy and produced the baseline output files the report names.
Every protected invariant has a measured baseline value with its query and derivation path, and one of them was reproduced through a second path.
doesNotProve: That the copy behaves like the production pipeline, or that the snapshot is the data production reads.
That a measured baseline is correct; it is what this pipeline produces today, not a verified truth.
That the discovered list of downstream consumers is complete.

checks.title: Pipeline change: review plan
checks.summary: Plans the requested change against the captured baseline: affected models, columns and consumers classified breaking, compatible or internal with reasons; ordered executable migration steps with their immediate checks and reversibility; and a rollback naming a preserved baseline, its possible data loss and its safe window. Every protected invariant carries forward its measured baseline and exact owner tolerance. The new behaviour must be observably false on the captured baseline, and the negative case names the invariants it should break before any result is seen.
checks.description:
Read ../profile/baseline-report.json and captured baseline outputs. Plan the requested change against those measured facts. Name affected models, columns and downstream consumers, following column changes through dependent models. Classify breaking, compatible or internal impacts with reasons; name consumers that cannot be checked. Provide executable ordered migration steps, immediate checks and reversibility. Rollback must name an existing preserved baseline or actual backup, state possible data loss and the safe rollback window. Do not implement yet.
Write change-plan.json as {impact:[{object:string,kind:"model"|"column"|"consumer",change:string,classification:"breaking"|"compatible"|"internal",why:string}],migrationSteps:[{step:string,command:string,reversible:boolean,verifyAfter:string}],rollback:{steps:[string],dataLoss:string,safeWindow:string},invariantImpact:[{invariant:exact declared name,measure:exact declared measure,kind:exact declared kind,unit:exact owner unit,tolerance:exact owner tolerance,baseline:typed captured baseline value,expected:"unchanged"|"within-tolerance",why:string}],newBehaviour:{statement:string,assertion:executable expression or query as a string,falseOnBaseline:string explaining how the captured baseline fails it},negativeCase:{change:string describing a reproducible mutation of a separate copy,expectedFailures:[exact declared invariant names]},consumerNotes:[string],safeUseNotes:string,rejectedAlternatives:[{alternative:string,whyRejected:string}]}.
Every declared invariant appears once, retaining its measured baseline and exact owner tolerance. Reject a requested change that necessarily contradicts an invariant; do not rewrite the invariant to make it pass. The new behavior must be observably false on captured baseline output and true after the change, so a no-op cannot pass. Name missing evidence rather than inventing it.
Before approval, describe the copied-data negative change and name its nonempty set of expected failing invariants. Each name must be a distinct declared invariant. Coupled measures may fail together; every invariant outside the approved set must still pass. These expectations are proposed by the agent for review, not independently supplied by the caller.
produces: change-plan.json : classified impact rows, ordered migration steps with commands, reversibility and post-checks, and a rollback with steps, data loss and safe window.
invariantImpact[] : every declared invariant once, with its captured baseline value, exact owner tolerance and why it will hold.
newBehaviour : the executable statement and assertion, plus how the captured baseline output fails it.
negativeCase : the reproducible mutation of a separate copy and the distinct set of declared invariants it is expected to fail.
recomputes: Requires every declared invariant to appear exactly once, retaining the measured baseline value and the exact owner tolerance.
Requires an executable new-behaviour statement, its assertion and an explanation of how the captured baseline fails it.
Requires a nonempty, distinct set of expected failing invariants, each a declared invariant name, fixed before anything is executed.
Requires classified impacts with reasons, ordered migration steps with commands and post-checks, and a rollback with steps, data loss and safe window.
Implements nothing: the plan waits for approval.
proves: The change is described against measured baseline values rather than remembered ones.
The negative case's expected failures were committed before any result was seen.
doesNotProve: That the migration steps work, that the rollback is possible, or that the impact list is complete.
That the new-behaviour assertion captures what the owner actually wanted.
That these expectations are independent: they are the agent's proposal for human review, not caller-supplied facts.

checks.title: Pipeline change: check results
checks.summary: Implements the approved change in its own copy, runs it against the same original data snapshot, and re-executes every protected invariant, the approved new-behaviour assertion, the grain checks and an independent re-derivation. A separate copied-data fixture, broken the approved way, must fail exactly the approved set of invariants and pass the rest. Migration and rollback are delivered as instructions; nothing is applied to the original source.
checks.description:
Read ../profile/baseline-report.json, its captured outputs, and ../rules/change-plan.json. Implement the approved change in this step's own copy, keeping every prior artifact unchanged. Deliver every added or modified model/script under models/ (SQL or the pipeline's native format), noting what changed and its approved migration step. Write manifest.json as {models:[{name:string,file:"models/<file>",status:"added"|"modified"|"unchanged",changedColumns:[string]}],migrationSteps:exact approved array,rollback:exact approved object,toolchain:{runtime:string,packages:[{name,version}]}}. Include migration and rollback instructions, but do not apply them to the original source. Deliver only safe-use-approved models; staging belongs in a separate working database or must be removed before sealing.
Create checks.sh that runs the changed pipeline on the SAME declared original data snapshot, executes EVERY invariant and the approved new-behavior assertion, checks the grain and independently re-derives at least one invariant from raw data using a separate parse path. Use captured baseline outputs to evaluate the same new-behavior assertion on the old result; it must be false there and true on the changed output. No primary evidence may come from synthetic fixtures. If the original source snapshot changed, fail and request a new baseline.
Make a separate copied-data broken-invariant fixture using the approved negativeCase.change. It must fail exactly the approved negativeCase.expectedFailures set and pass every other protected invariant. Do not select or adjust that set after seeing results. Run the SAME regression functions on the changed real output and this copied negative case. If the fixture passes everything, or the regression cannot run, checks.sh fails. Store the fixture and exact reproduction instructions. The fixture is model-authored; do not label it caller-fixed.
Write regression-report.json as {baselineRef:"../profile/baseline-report.json",snapshotIdentity:exact original snapshot identity,invariants:[RESULT],changeAssertion:{statement:exact approved statement,assertion:exact approved expression,observed:string,passOnBaseline:false,passOnChanged:true,pass:true},grainCheck:{grain:exact input grain,keyColumns:[exact candidates],duplicateRows:0,nullKeyRows:0,pass:true},independentControl:{invariant:one declared name,value:typed independent value,path:string different from result derivationPath,query:string},negativeCase:{id:"broken-invariant-fixture",whatWasBroken:exact approved negativeCase.change,query:string,tripped:true,invariants:[RESULT for every invariant]},consumersChecked:[{consumer:string,result:string}],passed:integer,failed:integer,timing:{budget:string,stages:[{stage:string,seconds:number}],withinBudget:boolean}}.
RESULT is {invariant:exact declared name,measure:exact declared measure,kind:exact declared kind,unit:exact owner unit,tolerance:exact owner tolerance,expected:typed captured baseline value,observed:typed measured value,delta:exact decimal string for observed minus expected for numbers or null for boolean/text,pass:computed boolean,query:string,derivationPath:string}. Absolute/count boundaries are inclusive. Percent_of_baseline uses the absolute captured baseline value; zero allows only zero difference. Exact means equality. The original baseline expected value and owner tolerance stay identical in real and negative results. The host independently recomputes each negative verdict from reported measurements and owner tolerances, then compares the failing invariant names with the exact approved set, regardless of order. Missing expected failures and additional failures both reject the check; primary results must all pass. This recomputation checks report arithmetic, not causal correctness of model-authored queries or fixtures. Top-level passed and failed count only the primary declared invariants: exclude behavior, grain, independent-control and negative-case checks from those two counts. Every discovered consumer is either checked or explicitly accounted for with missing evidence in its result, never silently omitted. Record actual row counts and relevant date/sequence bounds. checks.sh must exit nonzero for failed primary invariants, no-op behavior, invalid grain, missing execution or an undetected/badly targeted negative case. Print per-invariant results and their denominators. Run exactly sh checks.sh as a separate SDK command after all code edits, then only read results and hand off.
produces: models/<file> : every added or modified model or script, with its status and changed columns.
checks.sh : runs the changed pipeline on the same snapshot and executes every invariant, the change assertion, the grain check, the independent control and the negative fixture.
regression-report.json : invariant results with expected, observed and exact deltas; the assertion on baseline and changed output; the grain check; the independent control; the negative case.
manifest.json : the delivered models plus the approved migration steps and rollback, preserved exactly.
The copied-data broken-invariant fixture and its exact reproduction instructions, stored in this step.
recomputes: Observes the exact `sh checks.sh` execution and rejects a program or output inventory that changed around it.
Recomputes every invariant verdict from its expected and observed values under the exact owner tolerance, and the delta as observed minus baseline.
Requires expected values to come from the captured baseline and the same snapshot identity, and every protected invariant to pass.
Requires the approved assertion to be false on captured baseline output and true on changed output, so a no-op cannot pass.
Recomputes which invariants the negative fixture breaks and requires exactly the approved set, with every other invariant passing.
Requires the manifest to preserve the approved migration steps and rollback unchanged, with real model files delivered under models/.
Recomputes the independent control through a parse path different from the result's, and requires zero duplicate and zero null-key rows at the declared grain.
proves: The changed pipeline ran against the same snapshot and every protected invariant still holds within its owner tolerance.
The approved new behaviour is observable on the changed output and absent from the captured baseline.
The regression program detected the approved breakage: the copied fixture failed exactly the invariants it was meant to.
doesNotProve: That the change is correct beyond the invariants someone declared; unprotected behaviour is not checked.
That the negative fixture establishes detection causally. It is model-authored and reported by the same program, and is never caller-fixed.
That the migration or rollback was performed; both are delivered as instructions, not applied.
That downstream consumers are unaffected: consumers that could not be checked are named, not covered.

checks.title: Data pipeline: measure inputs
checks.summary: Measures every declared source in full before any model exists: access, schema, identity, row counts, column types with null and distinct counts, candidate-key duplicates, timestamp bounds and lag evidence. Every declared measure is also computed independently from raw sources through a named parse path and executable query, so the finished pipeline is later compared against a control captured before it was built. Unavailable sources fail explicitly; totals are never inferred from column names.
checks.description:
Measure all declared sources BEFORE designing or building models. Read every source in full, verify access and schema, record source identities (hashes or versions), actual row counts, column types/null/distinct counts, candidate-key duplicate counts, timestamp bounds and lag evidence. Finished-table keys can be derived: do not assume they already exist in raw sources. Identify duplicates, encoding/timezone uncertainty, sentinel values, soft-deletes and test rows. Preserve sensitive-field rules; use counts or masked examples. Independently compute EVERY declared measure from raw sources using its business definition, with a named parse path and executable query. These controls are captured before the pipeline exists. Fail explicitly for unavailable sources or controls; never substitute synthetic data or infer totals from column names.
Write source-profile.json as {declaredSources:exact inputs.sources,sources:[{name:string,readPath:string,identity:string,verified:true,rows:nonnegative integer,scanned:"full",columns:[{name,type,nullCount,distinctCount}],candidateKeys:[{columns:[string],unique:boolean,duplicateRows:integer}],observedRange:string,observedLag:string,issues:[string]}],controls:[{measure:exact declared name,definition:exact definition,unit:exact owner unit,tolerance:decimal string,value:decimal string,query:string,derivationPath:string}],assumptions:[string],openQuestions:[string]}. Record missing timestamp evidence explicitly instead of fabricating a time. Zero-row sources are allowed if actually observed and disclosed. checks.sh must execute profiling and independent controls and write this report. Do not build the future pipeline in this step.
produces: checks.sh : executes the profiling and the independent controls and writes the profile.
source-profile.json sources[] : per source the read path, identity, verified full scan, rows, columns with null and distinct counts, candidate keys, observed range and lag, and issues.
controls[] : one independent control per declared measure, with its value, executable query and named raw-source parse path.
recomputes: Observes the exact `sh checks.sh` execution and rejects a program or output inventory that changed around it.
Requires the exact declared sources, each verified with a full scan, an identity, a read path and an observed row count.
Rejects column null or distinct counts larger than the source row count, and a candidate key whose unique flag disagrees with its duplicate count.
Requires one independent control per declared measure, preserving the owner's definition, unit and tolerance, with an executed query and a named parse path.
proves: Every declared source was read in full and measured, and every requested measure has a control value captured before the pipeline existed.
Finished-table keys were measured rather than assumed to already exist in raw data.
doesNotProve: That the control values are correct: they are the model's own computation, checked for shape and arithmetic, not for truth.
That the sources are complete or current; observed range and lag are recorded as evidence, not validated.
That a source the profile never named is irrelevant.

checks.title: Data pipeline: review plan
checks.summary: Designs the simplest useful set of typed models from the measured sources: one named output model owning the declared finished grain and keys, each model's columns, materialization, build strategy and dependencies, and a map from every declared measure to its actual output column and expression, keeping the control captured at the profile step. Lag ceiling, refresh deadline and late-arrival behaviour stay separate declared facts, and missing optional policies stay undeclared. Nothing is implemented before approval.
checks.description:
Read PROFILE/source-profile.json. Design the simplest useful model dependencies from those measured facts. A single model may read sources directly; add preparation or intermediate models only when useful. Apply required confidential-field removal/masking before delivery. Name one outputModel that owns the declared finished grain and keys. Every measured source must contribute to that output through its declared dependencies; no staging/intermediate/mart layer taxonomy is required. Keep all requested measures and owner tolerances; preserve the already-measured independent controls. Do not implement before approval.
Write pipeline-plan.json as {targetStore:exact input targetStore,outputModel:approved finished model name,models:[{name:safe SQL identifier,grain:string,keyColumns:[string],upstreams:[{kind:"source"|"model",name:string}],columns:[{name:safe SQL identifier,type:string,description:string}],materialization:string,incrementalStrategy:string,tests:[string]}],measureMap:[{measure:declared name,definition:exact definition,unit:exact unit,tolerance:decimal string,model:outputModel name,column:actual output column,expression:string,exclusions:[string],controlQuery:exact profile control query,controlPath:exact profile control derivationPath}],freshness:{maxLag:exact input maxLag,refreshDeadline:input refreshDeadline or "",lateArrival:input lateArrival or "",verification:string,lateArrivalStrategy:string},safeUseNotes:string,publicationPlan:string,rejectedDesigns:[{design,whyRejected}]}.
Models are in dependency order. Source upstream names refer to the measured sources; model upstream names refer to earlier models. Upstreams are unique by kind and name; source and model names have separate namespaces. Keep lag ceiling, external refresh trigger/deadline and late-arrival/restatement behavior separate. Missing optional policies stay undeclared. Plan repeated builds so they do not duplicate or change results on unchanged input. Explain how actual freshness can be checked or what metadata is missing.
produces: pipeline-plan.json : the target store and the named output model, with 1-32 typed models in dependency order carrying columns, keys, upstreams, materialization, incremental strategy and tests.
measureMap[] : every declared measure mapped to its actual output column and expression, with the profile's control query and parse path preserved.
freshness, safeUseNotes, publicationPlan and rejectedDesigns : the declared timing facts, confidential-field handling, the delivery boundary and the designs that were rejected.
recomputes: Requires the requested target engine and one named output model carrying the declared grain and finished-table keys.
Walks the upstream graph and requires every measured source to contribute to the output model through declared dependencies; no layer naming scheme is accepted as coverage.
Requires each model's keys to exist among its own columns, and upstreams to be distinct and ordered after their sources and earlier models.
Requires every declared measure to map exactly once to a real output column, preserving the owner's definition, unit and tolerance and the profile's control query and path.
Requires maximum lag, refresh deadline and late-arrival policy to be kept as the exact declared facts, with a verification and a late-arrival strategy stated.
proves: The planned dependencies cover every measured source and terminate at one approved output model at the declared grain.
Every requested measure has a planned home and keeps its owner tolerance and its pre-existing independent control.
doesNotProve: That the SQL will produce correct results; no model has been built or executed at this step.
That the design is a good one, only that it is complete and internally consistent.
That the freshness contract can be met; the plan states how it would be checked.

checks.title: Data pipeline: check results
checks.summary: Builds the approved models against the full declared sources with the requested engine and verifies the result: source row accounting, grain uniqueness and non-null keys on the actual output, every measure reproduced against the control captured before the pipeline existed, a repeated build that changes nothing, the declared freshness behaviour, and a duplicate-key fixture the same assertion must reject. Delivery contains only the approved output model, and nothing is published or deployed to an external system.
checks.description:
Read PROFILE/source-profile.json and RULES/pipeline-plan.json as immutable inputs. Implement and EXECUTE the approved SQL against the full declared sources with the requested engine. Deliver flat models/<name>.sql files and checks.sql. Do not substitute an easier engine or fixture data for the real build; fail with the missing engine/access requirement when necessary. Write manifest.json as {targetStore:exact approved target,outputModel:exact approved outputModel,models:[each exact approved model object plus file:"models/<name>.sql"],toolchain:{runtime:string,packages:[{name,version}]}}. Deliver a native database or reloadable export under delivery/, containing only the approved outputModel. Other working tables stay in a separate working database or are removed from the delivery. Do not publish or deploy to an external system.
Run the same build twice on unchanged input and prove row count and every measure are unchanged. For source accounting, raw input rows equal retained source rows plus disjoint named exclusions; retained rows equal measured source contributions before aggregation. The final output row count is separate: grouping several source rows into one output row is legitimate. Execute grain uniqueness/non-null checks on actual output columns. Reproduce every control from the original raw source through its independent parse path; compare the output totals with those original controls using exact decimal arithmetic and the owner's unit/tolerance. Verify source identities still match the profile. Enforce declared lag/late-arrival behavior, including a late-row case when that policy was supplied; name missing timing metadata rather than claiming a schedule was installed.
Create a clean model-authored grain fixture and a copied variant with exactly one additional duplicate key. Run the SAME grain assertion on both. It must find zero duplicates/null keys in the clean seed and exactly one excess duplicate in the changed seed, with no null keys. Fixtures are additional controls, never primary evidence.
Write verification-report.json as {sources:[{name,identity,rows}],rowAccounting:[{source,inputRows,retainedRows,contributedRows,excluded:[{filter:string,rows:integer}],query:string}],grainCheck:{model:outputModel name,grain:exact owner grain,keyColumns:exact owner keys,rows:integer,duplicateRows:0,nullKeyRows:0,query:string},measures:[{measure,definition,unit,tolerance,expected:original control value,reproducedControl:same value,observed:output total,delta:observed minus expected,controlQuery:original control query,controlPath:original control path,modelPath:different actual SQL/model parse path,pass:true}],negativeCase:{source:"model-fixture",file:"fixtures/<file>",query:exact grain query,baseline:{rows:positive integer,duplicateRows:0,nullKeyRows:0},mutated:{rows:baseline plus one,duplicateRows:1,nullKeyRows:0},detected:true},publication:{file:"delivery/<database or export>",tables:[outputModel name],query:string},replay:{rowsBefore:output row count,rowsAfter:same,measuresBefore:[{measure,value}],measuresAfter:[{measure,value}],query:string,pass:true},freshness:{maxLag:exact input,refreshDeadline:input or "",lateArrival:input or "",observed:string,query:string,pass:true,lateCase:{performed:boolean,observation:string,query:string,pass:boolean}},checks:[{id:"row-accounting"|"key-uniqueness"|"measure-reproduction"|"negative-duplicate-key",pass:true,expected:string,observed:string,query:string}],passed:4,failed:0,timing:{budget:string,stages:[{stage:string,seconds:number}],withinBudget:true}}.
Top-level passed/failed count exactly the FOUR named check families, excluding replay and freshness checks. Every measure value/delta/tolerance is a full-precision decimal string. Absolute/count thresholds are inclusive; percent_of_control uses the absolute captured control, with zero permitting zero difference only. Preserve each approved measure definition and tolerance. A missing late-arrival policy means lateCase.performed:false with its absence explained, not an invented policy. For a declared policy execute the scenario and report pass:true with the reproduction query. checks.sh must execute every assertion, both builds and controls, print the measured counts, and exit nonzero on a failed check, source change, missed control or declared runtime overrun. Do not meet a budget by sampling, dropping checks or relaxing tolerances.

checks.sh : runs the build, the verification checks, the repeat build and the fixtures.
manifest.json : the approved target and output model with the exact approved model definitions and their files, plus the pinned runtime and package versions.
verification-report.json : executed sources, row accounting, grain check, measure results with deltas, negative case, publication, replay, freshness, the four check families and stage timings.

delivery/<file> : a native database or reloadable export containing only the approved output model.
recomputes: Observes the exact `sh checks.sh` execution and rejects a program or output inventory that changed around it.
Requires the build to read the same source identities and row counts the profile measured, with retained rows plus disjoint named exclusions equal to the input rows.
Recomputes each measure's delta as observed minus the captured control and requires it within that measure's own unit and tolerance, in exact decimal arithmetic.
Requires the output grain check to report zero duplicate and zero null-key rows on the declared keys, with its query recorded.
Requires a repeated build to preserve the row count and every measured total.
Requires the duplicate-key fixture to yield exactly one excess duplicate under the same grain assertion, and the delivery to contain only the approved output model.
Requires the declared freshness contract, executing a late-arrival case only when a policy was declared and refusing an invented one.
Requires exactly four executed, passing check families with evidence, and measured stage times within the declared budget.

Each delivered measure reproduces the control captured before the pipeline existed, within the owner's tolerance and in exact decimal arithmetic.
The finished table is unique and non-null at its declared grain, and a repeated build changed nothing.

That the fixtures establish detection causally; they are model-authored additional controls and never primary evidence.
That the pipeline will keep working on new data, or that any freshness policy is installed anywhere.

checks.title: Recompute prediction metrics
checks.summary: Recomputes the declared primary metric from the submitted predictions with trusted host code, then binds the result to the threshold and comparator on row one of the declared success metric, to the identity of the scored file, and to the reported evaluation set. Leakage checks and their seeded control are reported by the harness and carried through into a host-written score report that records, explicitly, what custody the check does not establish.
checks.description:
Produce predictions.csv with the exact header y_true,y_score and optional third column slice, one row per scored example. Binary labels are 0/1 with 1 positive; scores must be finite. Write eval-report.json with primaryMetric:{name,value,threshold,comparator,pass:true}, evalset:{sha256,rows}, and leakageChecks:[{id,pass:true,...}]. The primary metric is row ONE of the declared successMetric table, never a later metric. Retain its exact threshold and comparator (>=, >, <=, < or =); an explicit comparison direction is required; a bare numeric threshold is rejected. Accuracy and F1 need the declared operating point. Record the real evaluation-set SHA256 and exact prediction row count. If the owner names a holdout hash, it must match that holdout, not a development set. If a predictionsSha256 is reported, it must hash the actual predictions.csv.
Create checks.sh that executes the task's evaluation and requested checks using the supplied data and permissions. Run exactly sh checks.sh as a separate SDK command after every code edit, then only read and hand off. A successful exit means the evaluation and required checks completed. Do not replace declared data with synthetic fixtures; controlled variants are additional checks. Include at least one separately seeded post-label-feature leakage control with {id,pass:true,expectedTrip:true,tripped:true,evidence:string}; run the same leakage checks against that variant and keep it out of primary predictions. Every declared control must match its expected outcome, and every reported leakage check must pass. Name missing data, dependencies or failed checks instead of inventing results.
The host recomputes AUROC, PR-AUC (average precision), accuracy or F1 from submitted predictions, checks report agreement within 1e-6, and applies the declared comparison exactly without an epsilon. It observes the SDK command and pins artifacts; it never executes model-written programs as trusted host code. score-report.json is reserved for the host: do not create it. The host writes it only after acceptance. This check does not choose an algorithm or plan the workflow. It recomputes submitted labels and scores; it does not establish label/holdout custody, train/holdout isolation, split correctness or frozen-model provenance. Hash matching binds the report to a declared fingerprint, not the predictions to independent labels. Leakage-control fields remain harness-reported evidence requiring review. Preserve these limitations in the handoff and do not claim leakage protection or model provenance from this check alone.
produces: predictions.csv : the exact header y_true,y_score with an optional slice column, one row per scored example, 0/1 labels with 1 positive, and finite scores.
eval-report.json : primaryMetric with name, value, threshold, comparator and pass; evalset sha256 and rows; and leakageChecks including a seeded control with expectedTrip and tripped.
checks.sh : runs the evaluation and requested checks; run exactly `sh checks.sh` as a separate SDK command after every edit.
score-report.json is reserved for the host and written by it; the step must not create that file.
recomputes: Observes the exact `sh checks.sh` execution and rejects a program or output inventory that changed around it.
Rescores predictions.csv with trusted host code and rejects a reported value that disagrees with the recomputed one.
Recomputes the threshold comparison itself in exact decimal arithmetic using the declared comparator.
Requires the reported metric family, comparator and threshold to be exactly those declared on row one; a harness cannot set its own bar.
Re-hashes predictions.csv after scoring and rejects a file that changed, or a reported prediction identity that differs.
Requires the reported evaluation-set fingerprint to be a SHA-256 and to match a holdout hash the owner declared, when one was declared.
Requires every reported leakage check to have a distinct identity and pass, including a seeded control whose expectedTrip equals its tripped value.
Writes score-report.json itself, recording the binding and its explicit custody limitations.
proves: The submitted predictions really do produce the reported metric value: the host recomputed it and compared it against the declared threshold.
The scored file is the file that was hashed, and the reported evaluation set matches the declared holdout when one was declared.
doesNotProve: Label or holdout custody: nothing here establishes where y_true came from.
Train/holdout isolation, split correctness, or that a frozen model produced these scores.
That the leakage controls ran as described; they are reported by the harness and recorded as reported, not verified.
That the evaluated population is complete or representative: the rows scored are the rows submitted.
